thread:
incident-bot: SEV2: p99 latency spike for streaming API in shared-gpu pool (alerts: latency-p99 > 1.2s for 3m) -- paging oncall

oncall-ryan: paging in. seeing automated SLO alert, pulling up dashboards.

alex: I can repro in the realtime dashboard — streaming p95 ~ 300ms, p99 jumped to ~1.6s. Spikes align with high nvme writeback on hosts gpu-pool-47/48.

maria: customer visible? any 500s or just slower streams?

alex: no 5xxs, just stalled chunks. some clients report UI stalls for ~2s during generation. CS ticket #5371 from AcmeCorp reporting degraded UX.

jin: looking at cgroup metrics on gpu-pool-47: blkio.throttle.io_serviced shows large write latency and write bytes out during spike. NVMe queue depth high.

sam: likely noisy neighbor causing writeback pressure; shared pool. Are there recent large embeddings/backup jobs scheduled?

nina: checking job-scheduler — big batch export started 10:12 UTC on tenant t-acme-export (owner: data-exports). It uses host-affinity to gpu-pool-47.

oncall-ryan: good find. Impact path: writeback IO -> NVMe saturation -> host IO wait -> process stalls -> streaming stalls -> p99 spikes. Immediate mitigation options?

alex: short-term: throttle/evict the export job from shared pool, or reduce blkio weight for that tenant container to lower IO priority. We have a spare host in spare-pool for live-migrate.

maria: recommend evict + move to dedicated burst node for the export. CS: we should message AcmeCorp with a quick note — "we're investigating intermittent streaming slowness".

cs-liaison: I'm on it, sending a customer status now: "We're investigating intermittent slowdowns affecting streaming generation; engineers are mitigating and we'll update shortly." :+1:

jin: I can run live cgroup tweak first to reduce immediate pressure, command below. This is less disruptive than eviction:

```
# on host gpu-pool-47
echo 500 > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/containers/t-acme-export/blkio.weight
```

but kernel behavior varies; may not fully remove queueing.

oncall-ryan: do it, but keep eviction as plan B. Apply throttle and watch p99. Set a 3min checkpoint.

alex: applying cgroup change now, tailing streaming worker logs and nvme stats.

(30s later) alex: nvme write queue depth down ~60%, p99 dropped to 950ms from 1.6s. Still above target but trending down.

sam: if it holds, we can avoid migration. But export job will still cause intermittent bursts. We should schedule a background move to spare-pool and limit concurrent export concurrency to 1.

nina: I have spare-pool hosts ready. I'll start live-migrate via orchestrator with graceful shutdown on the export container. Command:

```
orchestrator migrate --tenant t-acme-export --from gpu-pool-47 --to spare-pool-12 --grace 60s
```

oncall-ryan: proceed. Keep me posted. Also create a short-term firewall to prevent new large batch jobs getting scheduled to shared pool.

maria: created a scheduling hold on tenant t-acme-export for shared-gpu pool. will remove once migration completes.

(2m later) alex: migration kicked, container drained gracefully. After migration p99 back to 220ms, p95 stable. NVMe queues returned to normal on gpu-pool-47.

eng-sre: adding a followup action: we should add an autoscheduler rule to avoid colocating large batch exporters with low-latency streaming tenants. Filing ENG-1289.

oncall-ryan: agree. Immediate mitigations complete. We'll keep monitoring for 30m. Ryan -> handing off to eng-sre for post-incident followup. Oncall clear from paging but remain available.

cs-liaison: updated AcmeCorp: "We moved a background export job off the shared pool which resolved the streaming slowdowns. We'll follow up with a postmortem and preventive changes."

maria: quick notes for postmortem: root cause = noisy multi-tenant export causing NVMe writeback saturation on shared-pool hosts -> cgroup blkio limits insufficient by default -> streaming process stalls at host IO wait -> p99 spike. Mitigations applied: immediate blkio weight tweak, migration to spare host, scheduling hold. Actions: ENG-1289 scheduler rule; measure blkio thresholds and set alert on nvme queue depth; consider per-tenant IO caps for shared pool.

oncall-ryan: closing thread; monitor until 6162626298. :white_check_mark:
